axis: breach notification window: large-scale (500+ individuals) breach vs small-scale breach, individual notification deadline in days
rule_template: A covered entity experiencing <<CATEGORY_A>> breach of unsecured protected health information must notify affected individuals within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of discovery, and a covered entity experiencing <<CATEGORY_B>> breach of unsecured protected health information must notify affected individuals within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of discovery.
scenario_template_a: Rosewood Regional Medical Center discovered on March 3 that an unencrypted laptop containing patient billing records had been stolen from a locked office. The center's privacy officer determined the incident affected 1,150 patients across three clinics. The compliance team began mailing individual notification letters <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the date of discovery.
scenario_template_b: Pinehill Family Practice discovered on March 3 that an unencrypted laptop containing patient billing records had been stolen from a locked office. The practice's privacy officer determined the incident affected 42 patients at the single-location clinic. The compliance team began mailing individual notification letters <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the date of discovery.

axis: patient right-of-access response deadline: electronic portal-based records vs paper-based legacy records, in days
rule_template: A covered entity responding to an individual's request for access to <<CATEGORY_A>> records must provide the requested records within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of receiving the request, and a covered entity responding to an individual's request for access to <<CATEGORY_B>> records must provide the requested records within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of receiving the request.
scenario_template_a: Harbor View Medical Group received a written request from a patient asking for a full copy of her records, which are maintained entirely within the practice's certified electronic health record system. The health information management department logged the request on June 2 and began compiling the electronic file. Staff completed and delivered the records to the patient <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the request was logged.
scenario_template_b: Harbor View Medical Group received a written request from a patient asking for a full copy of her records, which are maintained entirely on paper in the practice's legacy chart storage room. The health information management department logged the request on June 2 and began locating the paper file. Staff completed and delivered the records to the patient <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the request was logged.

axis: security risk analysis review cycle: high-risk information system vs low-risk information system, review interval in months
rule_template: A covered entity operating <<CATEGORY_A>> information system must conduct a documented security risk analysis review at least every <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and a covered entity operating <<CATEGORY_B>> information system must conduct a documented security risk analysis review at least every <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: Cedarbrook Health Network classified its patient portal server, which stores payment card data alongside PHI and accepts external logins, as a system carrying elevated exposure to unauthorized access. The IT security team scheduled its documented risk analysis reviews for this server at intervals of <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_b: Cedarbrook Health Network classified its internal scheduling server, which stores appointment metadata only and has no external network access, as a system carrying limited exposure to unauthorized access. The IT security team scheduled its documented risk analysis reviews for this server at intervals of <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.

axis: audit log retention period: systems storing psychotherapy notes vs systems storing general clinical records, in years
rule_template: A covered entity maintaining audit logs for systems that store <<CATEGORY_A>> must retain those audit logs for at least <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and a covered entity maintaining audit logs for systems that store <<CATEGORY_B>> must retain those audit logs for at least <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: Lakeside Behavioral Health Associates operates a dedicated software module in which its therapists record session notes documenting the content of patient counseling conversations, separate from the shared clinical chart. The organization's IT policy set the audit log retention period for this module's server at <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_b: Lakeside Behavioral Health Associates operates a standard electronic health record module in which its clinicians record vital signs, diagnoses, and medication orders as part of the shared clinical chart. The organization's IT policy set the audit log retention period for this module's server at <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.

axis: de-identification safe harbor: number of identifier categories removed under the Safe Harbor method vs the Limited Data Set method
rule_template: A covered entity de-identifying a dataset under the <<CATEGORY_A>> method must remove at least <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of direct and indirect patient identifiers, and a covered entity de-identifying a dataset under the <<CATEGORY_B>> method must remove at least <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of direct and indirect patient identifiers.
scenario_template_a: Meridian Health Analytics prepared a research dataset intended for public release with no data use agreement restricting the recipient, drawing from five years of oncology visit records. The data governance team stripped identifier fields from the export and logged that the final file had <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> removed before the dataset was released.
scenario_template_b: Meridian Health Analytics prepared a research dataset intended for release to a university research partner under a signed data use agreement, drawing from five years of oncology visit records. The data governance team stripped identifier fields from the export and logged that the final file had <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> removed before the dataset was released.

axis: incidental disclosure exception: minimum physical separation distance in a high-volume walk-in setting vs a scheduled appointment-based setting, in feet
rule_template: A covered entity operating <<CATEGORY_A>> care setting must maintain at least <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of separation between patient check-in conversation areas and the public waiting area to rely on the incidental disclosure exception, and a covered entity operating <<CATEGORY_B>> care setting must maintain at least <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of separation between patient check-in conversation areas and the public waiting area to rely on the incidental disclosure exception.
scenario_template_a: Sunview Urgent Care redesigned its front desk after noticing that unscheduled patients frequently queued within earshot of the intake counter during peak afternoon hours. The facilities team measured the renovated layout and confirmed that the check-in counter sits <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> from the nearest waiting area seating.
scenario_template_b: Bellmont Specialty Clinic redesigned its front desk after noticing that patients arriving for scheduled appointments occasionally lingered near the intake counter before being called back. The facilities team measured the renovated layout and confirmed that the check-in counter sits <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> from the nearest waiting area seating.

axis: IRB continuing review interval for authorization waiver: expedited-review research protocol vs full-board-review research protocol, in months
rule_template: An institutional review board overseeing <<CATEGORY_A>> research protocol that waives individual authorization for use of protected health information must conduct continuing review at least every <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and an institutional review board overseeing <<CATEGORY_B>> research protocol that waives individual authorization for use of protected health information must conduct continuing review at least every <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: Dr. Amara Osei's retrospective chart-review study of diabetes medication adherence was classified by the university IRB as posing no more than minimal risk to subjects and involving only existing records. The IRB approved a waiver of authorization for the study and scheduled its continuing review at intervals of <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_b: Dr. Amara Osei's prospective study testing a novel insulin delivery device was classified by the university IRB as involving direct subject interaction and physiological monitoring. The IRB approved a waiver of authorization for the study and scheduled its continuing review at intervals of <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.

axis: marketing authorization threshold: financially remunerated communication vs non-remunerated communication, payment amount in dollars
rule_template: A covered entity sending <<CATEGORY_A>> marketing communication in which it receives more than <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> in payment from a third party per communication must obtain prior written authorization from the individual, and a covered entity sending <<CATEGORY_B>> marketing communication in which it receives more than <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> in payment from a third party per communication must obtain prior written authorization from the individual.
scenario_template_a: Fairhaven Pharmacy Chain entered into a promotional arrangement with a pharmaceutical manufacturer under which the manufacturer pays the pharmacy for each mailer sent to patients currently prescribed a competing diabetes medication, encouraging them to ask their doctor about the manufacturer's brand. The pharmacy's finance department recorded that the manufacturer pays <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> per mailer sent.
scenario_template_b: Fairhaven Pharmacy Chain entered into a promotional arrangement with a pharmaceutical manufacturer under which the manufacturer pays the pharmacy for each mailer sent to patients currently prescribed a refill-eligible generic medication, reminding them that a refill is due. The pharmacy's finance department recorded that the manufacturer pays <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> per mailer sent.

axis: authorization validity period: research-related disclosure vs treatment-related disclosure, in years
rule_template: A signed authorization for <<CATEGORY_A>> disclosure of protected health information remains valid for up to <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> from the date of signature unless the individual revokes it sooner, and a signed authorization for <<CATEGORY_B>> disclosure of protected health information remains valid for up to <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> from the date of signature unless the individual revokes it sooner.
scenario_template_a: A participant in Northfield University's longitudinal cardiovascular study signed an authorization permitting the study team to pull her clinic records for the biobank registry tied to the study. The consent form she signed on January 10, 2023 specified a validity period of <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> from the signature date.
scenario_template_b: A patient at Northfield Orthopedic Associates signed an authorization permitting her prior physical therapy provider to release her treatment records to her new orthopedic surgeon. The consent form she signed on January 10, 2023 specified a validity period of <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> from the signature date.

axis: verbal consent reconfirmation interval for facility directory listing: inpatient encounter vs outpatient encounter, in days
rule_template: For <<CATEGORY_A>> encounter, a patient's verbal permission to be listed in the facility directory remains effective for <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> before staff must reconfirm it, and for <<CATEGORY_B>> encounter, a patient's verbal permission to be listed in the facility directory remains effective for <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> before staff must reconfirm it.
scenario_template_a: When Mr. Delgado was admitted to Prairie View Hospital for a multi-day stay following surgery, the admitting nurse verbally asked whether he wished to be listed in the hospital directory so visitors and callers could be told his room number. He agreed, and the front desk's log shows his directory listing remained active for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> without staff re-asking him.
scenario_template_b: When Ms. Delgado came to Prairie View Clinic for a same-day outpatient procedure, the front-desk clerk verbally asked whether she wished to be listed in the clinic directory so visitors and callers could be told she was on-site. She agreed, and the front desk's log shows her directory listing remained active for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> without staff re-asking her.

axis: minor's independent authorization age: substance-use-disorder treatment records vs general medical records, in years
rule_template: A minor patient may independently authorize disclosure of their <<CATEGORY_A>> records without parental consent upon reaching <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of age, and a minor patient may independently authorize disclosure of their <<CATEGORY_B>> records without parental consent upon reaching <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of age.
scenario_template_a: A 15-year-old patient at Elmwood Adolescent Health Center sought outpatient counseling for substance use on his own, without a parent present, and asked the clinic to send his session records to a school counselor for coordination of support services. The intake coordinator noted the patient's age as <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> at the time he signed the release himself.
scenario_template_b: A 15-year-old patient at Elmwood Adolescent Health Center visited for a routine sports physical and asked the clinic to send his general exam results to a school coach for an athletics eligibility file. The intake coordinator noted the patient's age as <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> at the time he signed the release himself.

axis: subcontractor breach reporting chain: business associate vs subcontractor of a business associate, reporting deadline in days
category_b: a subcontractor of a business associate
rule_template: Acting as <<CATEGORY_A>>, an entity discovering a breach of unsecured protected health information must report the breach upstream within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of discovery, and acting as <<CATEGORY_B>>, an entity discovering a breach of unsecured protected health information must report the breach upstream within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of discovery.
scenario_template_a: CloudChart Systems, which hosts electronic health record infrastructure directly for Willowbrook Clinic under a signed business associate agreement, detected unusual login activity indicating a breach affecting patient records stored on its servers. CloudChart's security team completed its internal investigation and reported the incident to Willowbrook Clinic <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the activity was first detected.
scenario_template_b: DataSecure Billing, a subcontractor hired by CloudChart Systems to process overflow claims transactions on CloudChart's behalf, detected unusual login activity indicating a breach affecting patient records it processes for CloudChart. DataSecure's security team completed its internal investigation and reported the incident to CloudChart Systems <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the activity was first detected.

axis: post-termination PHI return/destruction deadline: business associate vs subcontractor, in days
rule_template: Upon termination of its agreement, <<CATEGORY_A>> must return or destroy all protected health information in its possession within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of termination, and upon termination of its agreement, <<CATEGORY_B>> must return or destroy all protected health information in its possession within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of termination.
scenario_template_a: Vantage Transcription Services held a direct business associate agreement with Oakridge Medical Group to transcribe dictated physician notes into the electronic record. When Oakridge ended the contract on September 1 to move transcription in-house, Vantage's data management team completed the return of all patient files to Oakridge <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the termination date.
scenario_template_b: Relay Transcription Partners was engaged by Vantage Transcription Services as a subcontractor to handle overflow dictation files originating from Oakridge Medical Group. When Vantage ended its arrangement with Relay on September 1 to consolidate work internally, Relay's data management team completed the return of all patient files to Vantage <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the termination date.

axis: OCR document production deadline during compliance review: covered entity vs business associate, in days
rule_template: When OCR issues a document request during a compliance review, <<CATEGORY_A>> must produce the requested records within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of the request, and when OCR issues a document request during a compliance review, <<CATEGORY_B>> must produce the requested records within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of the request.
scenario_template_a: Brightpath Family Medicine, the physician practice that directly treats and bills patients, received a document request from the HHS Office for Civil Rights as part of a routine compliance review following a patient complaint. The practice's compliance officer logged the request on April 4 and assembled the requested policies and training records, submitting the completed response <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> later.
scenario_template_b: ClaimsFlow Processing, the third-party billing vendor that Brightpath Family Medicine contracts with to submit insurance claims, received a document request from the HHS Office for Civil Rights as part of a routine compliance review following a patient complaint. The vendor's compliance officer logged the request on April 4 and assembled the requested policies and training records, submitting the completed response <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> later.

axis: medical record retention after last service date: adult patient vs minor patient, in years
rule_template: A covered entity must retain the medical records of <<CATEGORY_A>> patient for at least <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> after the last date of service, and a covered entity must retain the medical records of <<CATEGORY_B>> patient for at least <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> after the last date of service.
scenario_template_a: Riverton Pediatric and Family Clinic closed the chart of a 45-year-old patient after her final visit on August 12, 2016, once she transferred her care to a new provider in another state. The clinic's records retention schedule requires the chart to remain in storage for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> from that final visit date.
scenario_template_b: Riverton Pediatric and Family Clinic closed the chart of a 9-year-old patient after his final visit on August 12, 2016, once his family transferred his care to a new provider in another state. The clinic's records retention schedule requires the chart to remain in storage for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> from that final visit date.

axis: records request response deadline: minor patient's guardian requester vs incapacitated adult patient's guardian requester, in days
rule_template: A covered entity responding to <<CATEGORY_A>> records request must provide the records within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of receiving the request, and a covered entity responding to <<CATEGORY_B>> records request must provide the records within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of receiving the request.
scenario_template_a: The mother of a 6-year-old patient at Thornwood Pediatrics submitted a written request for a complete copy of her son's immunization and visit history to share with his new school. The clinic's records department logged the request on October 1 and delivered the completed file to her <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> later.
scenario_template_b: The court-appointed guardian of a 68-year-old patient with advanced dementia at Thornwood Senior Care submitted a written request for a complete copy of his medication and visit history to share with a new long-term care facility. The clinic's records department logged the request on October 1 and delivered the completed file to her <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> later.

axis: advance notice before facility transfer disclosure: incarcerated patient vs non-incarcerated patient, in hours
rule_template: Before transferring custody of <<CATEGORY_A>> patient, a covered entity may disclose the patient's location and health status to the receiving facility with as little as <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of advance notice, and before transferring custody of <<CATEGORY_B>> patient, a covered entity may disclose the patient's location and health status to the receiving facility with as little as <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of advance notice.
scenario_template_a: Cascade Regional Medical Center coordinated the transfer of an inmate patient back to the county correctional facility after he completed treatment for a fractured wrist. The hospital's discharge planning team notified the correctional facility's medical unit of the transfer and shared his treatment summary <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> before he was picked up.
scenario_template_b: Cascade Regional Medical Center coordinated the transfer of a non-incarcerated patient to a skilled nursing facility after he completed treatment for a fractured wrist. The hospital's discharge planning team notified the nursing facility's admissions unit of the transfer and shared his treatment summary <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> before he was picked up.

axis: fitness-for-duty determination reporting deadline: active-duty armed forces patient vs civilian patient, in days
rule_template: A covered entity evaluating <<CATEGORY_A>> patient's fitness for duty must report the determination to the requesting authority within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of the evaluation, and a covered entity evaluating <<CATEGORY_B>> patient's fitness for duty must report the determination to the requesting authority within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of the evaluation.
scenario_template_a: Naval Medical Readiness Clinic conducted a fitness-for-duty evaluation on an active-duty sailor referred by his commanding officer following a shoulder injury during training. The examining physician completed the evaluation on May 5 and transmitted the duty-status determination to the requesting authority <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> later.
scenario_template_b: Lakeshore Occupational Health Clinic conducted a fitness-for-duty evaluation on a civilian warehouse employee referred by his employer following a shoulder injury during a shift. The examining physician completed the evaluation on May 5 and transmitted the duty-status determination to the requesting authority <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> later.

axis: minimum necessary look-back scope: payment-related disclosure request vs healthcare-operations-related disclosure request, in years
rule_template: When responding to <<CATEGORY_A>> disclosure request, a covered entity may release up to <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of historical records without seeking additional patient authorization, and when responding to <<CATEGORY_B>> disclosure request, a covered entity may release up to <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of historical records without seeking additional patient authorization.
scenario_template_a: Glenview Orthopedic Group received a request from a patient's insurer seeking her treatment history to adjudicate a claim for a recent knee replacement surgery. The billing office compiled records dating back <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> from the request to support the claim review.
scenario_template_b: Glenview Orthopedic Group received a request from its own quality improvement committee seeking a patient's treatment history to include in a surgical outcomes review as part of the practice's internal case-review process. The quality office compiled records dating back <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> from the request to support the review.

axis: opt-out compliance deadline: fundraising communication vs appointment-reminder communication, in days
rule_template: After receiving an individual's request to stop <<CATEGORY_A>> communication, a covered entity must cease sending that communication within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of the request, and after receiving an individual's request to stop <<CATEGORY_B>> communication, a covered entity must cease sending that communication within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of the request.
scenario_template_a: A former patient of Highland Health Foundation called the development office to ask that the hospital's annual giving campaign letters, which reference her past care to personalize the appeal, stop being mailed to her home. The development office logged her request on February 2 and confirmed her name was removed from the mailing list <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> later.
scenario_template_b: A current patient of Highland Health Foundation called the scheduling office to ask that the clinic's automated text messages reminding her of upcoming appointments stop being sent to her phone. The scheduling office logged her request on February 2 and confirmed her number was removed from the reminder system <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> later.

axis: accounting-of-disclosures look-back period: public-health-reporting disclosures vs judicial-or-administrative-proceeding disclosures, in years
rule_template: When compiling an accounting of disclosures upon patient request, a covered entity must include <<CATEGORY_A>> disclosures made within the preceding <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and when compiling an accounting of disclosures upon patient request, a covered entity must include <<CATEGORY_B>> disclosures made within the preceding <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: A patient at Fernwood County Health Department requested a full accounting of disclosures of her immunization records, which the health department had periodically reported to the state communicable disease registry as part of routine public health surveillance. The records office compiled a log covering disclosures made over the preceding <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_b: A patient at Fernwood County Health Department requested a full accounting of disclosures of her medical records, which the health department had released in response to a subpoena issued during a custody dispute proceeding. The records office compiled a log covering disclosures made over the preceding <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.

axis: Omnibus Rule transition grace period: legacy business associate agreement vs new business associate agreement, in days
category_a: a pre-Omnibus-Rule legacy business associate agreement
category_b: a post-Omnibus-Rule new business associate agreement
rule_template: A covered entity operating under <<CATEGORY_A>> has up to <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> after the compliance date to bring the agreement into conformance with the updated Rule, and a covered entity operating under <<CATEGORY_B>> has up to <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> after the compliance date to bring the agreement into conformance with the updated Rule.
scenario_template_a: Millbrook Health System had signed its business associate agreement with a claims-processing vendor in 2011, well before the Omnibus Rule's compliance date, and the agreement had not been set to renew or been modified since signing. The compliance department flagged the contract for updated breach-notification and subcontractor language and completed the amendment <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the compliance date.
scenario_template_b: Millbrook Health System signed a new business associate agreement with a claims-processing vendor shortly after the Omnibus Rule's compliance date, entering into the relationship for the first time under the updated framework. The compliance department drafted the agreement with updated breach-notification and subcontractor language and completed the agreement <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the compliance date.

axis: GINA remediation deadline: pre-GINA legacy health plan enrollment vs post-GINA new enrollment, in months
rule_template: A health plan administering benefits under <<CATEGORY_A>> must complete remediation of any underwriting documents that used genetic information within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of identifying the issue, and a health plan administering benefits under <<CATEGORY_B>> must complete remediation of any underwriting documents that used genetic information within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of identifying the issue.
scenario_template_a: Statewide Employer Health Plan discovered during an internal audit that an enrollee's 2008 underwriting file, opened before the plan updated its intake forms for GINA, contained a family medical history questionnaire referencing hereditary cancer risk. The compliance team began remediating the file and completed the correction <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the issue was identified.
scenario_template_b: Statewide Employer Health Plan discovered during an internal audit that an enrollee's 2015 underwriting file, opened after the plan updated its intake forms for GINA, contained a family medical history questionnaire referencing hereditary cancer risk. The compliance team began remediating the file and completed the correction <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the issue was identified.

axis: EHR migration cutover digitization deadline: records created before cutover vs records created after cutover, in months
category_a: records created before the EHR migration cutover date
category_b: records created after the EHR migration cutover date
rule_template: A covered entity must bring <<CATEGORY_A>> into the new system's standardized audit-trail format within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of the migration cutover, and a covered entity must bring <<CATEGORY_B>> into the new system's standardized audit-trail format within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of the migration cutover.
scenario_template_a: When Ashford Community Hospital completed its migration to a new electronic health record platform on January 15, its IT team began the project of scanning and indexing paper charts that had been created before the cutover so they would carry proper audit-trail metadata in the new system. The scanning and indexing project for these older charts was completed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the cutover date.
scenario_template_b: When Ashford Community Hospital completed its migration to a new electronic health record platform on January 15, its IT team began the project of validating audit-trail metadata for charts opened directly in the new system after the cutover date. The validation project for these newly created charts was completed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the cutover date.

axis: public health emergency waiver duration: facility inside declared disaster area vs affiliated facility outside declared disaster area, in hours
category_a: a facility located within the declared disaster area
category_b: an affiliated facility located outside the declared disaster area
rule_template: During a declared public health emergency, <<CATEGORY_A>> may rely on the Secretary's waiver of sanctions for specified HIPAA requirements for up to <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> after the disaster declaration, and during a declared public health emergency, <<CATEGORY_B>> may rely on the Secretary's waiver of sanctions for specified HIPAA requirements for up to <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> after the disaster declaration.
scenario_template_a: Following a declared public health emergency after a hurricane made landfall, Coastal Memorial Hospital, situated directly within the officially designated disaster area, began operating under emergency protocols including relaxed procedures for obtaining patient acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices. The hospital's emergency operations log shows these relaxed procedures remained in effect for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the disaster declaration was issued.
scenario_template_b: Following the same declared public health emergency after a hurricane made landfall, Piedmont Regional Medical Center, an affiliated hospital located outside the officially designated disaster area but part of the same health system, began operating under emergency protocols including relaxed procedures for obtaining patient acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices. The hospital's emergency operations log shows these relaxed procedures remained in effect for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the disaster declaration was issued.
